absent: Locking, interrupt safety and concurrency rules for hash, sparse, page-extension and slab paths.
Exact numeric encodings of hash flags, section markers, shifts and masks.
Internals of early reservation, virtual mapping, exact page allocation, leak tracking and logging services.
Command-line option names and registration binding the early boolean parsers.
Layout of page, folio, mem_section, usage descriptor, slab cache and sheaf structures beyond sizing and alignment rules observed.
Details of zonelist construction, huge-page reservation, vmemmap population, kfence, KMSAN, stack depot, page ownership and isolation finalization.
Failure handling beyond boot termination and warnings for the observed allocation paths.

findings.text: Provides a boot-time hash table allocator accepting a table name, bucket size, requested entry count, scale factor, behaviour flags, optional shift and mask outputs, and lower and upper entry bounds, returning the allocated table.

A zero requested count is derived from available kernel pages with megabyte granularity on small-page systems, adjusted by scale relative to page shift with extra widening on wide address spaces, forced to at least one page of buckets, normalized to a power of two, then clamped to caller limits, a default ceiling near one sixteenth of memory, and an absolute ceiling at two to the thirty-first entries.

Backing choice separates very early reservation with optional zeroing, virtual mapping with huge-page detection for oversized or distributed requests, and exact page allocation with leak tracking otherwise, retrying with successively smaller powers of two until one page remains and reporting identity, count, order, size and backing kind on success.
Failure to secure any backing after shrinking to the smallest permitted size terminates boot with a diagnostic identifying the table by name.

Three early command-line parsers record boolean requests for zeroing on allocation, zeroing on release, and page-content checking into early variables, returning the underlying text-to-boolean conversion status.

Hardening setup resolves interactions among poisoning, allocation and release zeroing, page-alloc debugging and guard pages, with a compatibility notice under a sanitizer runtime, enabling the corresponding runtime switches and enabling page checking whenever any relevant option or early request is active unless already covered by a debug build.
Startup reporting summarizes stack initialization mode alongside heap allocation and release zeroing states, warning that full memory clearing can be slow when release zeroing is active.

Early memory core bring-up establishes the shared zero page and its frame number through a weak architecture hook with a generic fallback, allows weak hooks for architecture preinit and low-level init, and prepares node areas, huge-page reservations, sparse bookkeeping and the page array.

Full memory initialization proceeds in broad phases: topology and per-CPU allocator state with debugging setup and early reporting, then release of early reservations and activation of the slab allocator with late page-extension and virtual-mapping services, finishing with isolation and cache finalization before non-init threads appear.

Sparse initialization records present ranges, validates descriptor sizing and alignment preconditions, then walks present sections in node-contiguous groups so each node range is initialized together, finishing with subsection presence and a final population summary.

Presence recording aligns each range to section boundaries, clamps it to the sparsemem addressable window, assigns a node identifier per section, and for newly seen sections encodes the early node id together with online and present marks.

Per-section page arrays are sized from descriptor size times pages per section, aligned to a large mapping granularity on one build and to page granularity on the other and reserved from boot memory, while per-section usage descriptors are bulk-allocated per node and consumed linearly with a bounds check.

Subsection presence is built by walking firmware-provided frame ranges and setting bitmap coverage per section, splitting ranges that cross section boundaries and noting the affected subsection indexes; a header variant provides an empty implementation when the feature is disabled.
Per-CPU page-allocator state registers online and offline hotplug callbacks under a dedicated hotplug step, warning if registration fails.

Flatmem page-extension storage is allocated per online node from boot memory with extra padding when node boundaries are unaligned to the largest buddy block, accounts total bytes, aborts on failure, and invokes registered need and init callbacks at setup and late stages.

Slab bring-up moves from static boot descriptors through a partial state to fully dynamic caches, establishing node sets, hotplug handling, sized allocation families, per-CPU sheaf structures and freelist randomization before reporting geometry.

Cache creation normalizes alignment from caller, hardware cache-line, architecture minimum and pointer-size constraints with special power-of-two handling for sized caches, exempts boot caches from merging, bounds partial lists by object size, provisions per-CPU sheaf state and NUMA defrag defaults, prepares randomized freelists once operational, and attaches control interfaces only after the allocator is up, releasing partially built state on error.

Behaviour selectors include early versus dynamic hash backing with optional zeroing, section online and early markers with an encoded node field and section-aligned masks, and slab alignment and merging controls with sized-cache and debugging modifiers.

Unrecoverable boot-time failures in node usage allocation, section map allocation, page-extension allocation and boot-cache creation terminate execution, while out-of-window frame ranges are clamped with a one-time warning and descriptor-size violations are rejected at build time.

Several services have build-dependent duplicates: section-to-node recording versus empty, large-granularity versus page-granularity section sizing, wide versus narrow freelist atomic checks, and active versus empty sparse, sysfs and debugfs hooks, with per-node virtual-map setup delegating to huge-page early setup.
